stemMarkdown: Two runners start together from the same point on a circular track 1200 m long, running at 4.5 km/h and 6.5 km/h. After how many seconds will they both be at the starting point together again? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: Each runner is back at the start only after a whole number of laps. One lap takes $960.0000$ s and $664.6154$ s respectively, so they coincide at the start at the LCM of those two times: $8640.0$ seconds.
altSolutionMarkdown: This is different from simply meeting somewhere on the track — here both must be at the start line, so it is an LCM of lap times, not a relative-speed calculation.
